metadata.ground_truth_policy: expected_evidence is primary; expected_sources is fallback

cases.query: What is the territorial extent of the Information Technology Act, 2000?
expected_evidence: It shall extend to the whole of India

cases.query: What does access mean under the Information Technology Act, 2000?
expected_evidence: gaining entry into, instructing or communicating with the logical, arithmetical, or memory function resources of a computer

cases.query: What makes an electronic signature reliable under the Information Technology Act?
expected_evidence: the signature creation data or the authentication data are, within the context in which they are used, linked to the signatory

cases.query: When does the Information Technology Act recognize information as satisfying a writing requirement in electronic form?
expected_evidence: rendered or made available in an electronic form

cases.query: When is a signature requirement satisfied by an electronic signature?
expected_evidence: authenticated by means of electronic signature

cases.query: When is an electronic record dispatched under section 13?
expected_evidence: the dispatch of an electronic record occurs when it enters a computer resource outside the control of the originator

cases.query: When is an electronic record received if the addressee has designated a computer resource?
expected_evidence: receipt occurs at the time when the electronic record enters the designated computer resource

cases.query: When is an electronic record considered secure?
expected_evidence: such record shall be deemed to be a secure electronic record from such point of time to the time of verification

cases.query: What conditions make an electronic signature a secure electronic signature?
expected_evidence: the signature creation data, at the time of affixing signature, was under the exclusive control of signatory

cases.query: What must a subscriber do to generate a key pair?
expected_evidence: the subscriber shall generate that key pair by applying the security procedure

cases.query: When is a subscriber deemed to have accepted a Digital Signature Certificate?
expected_evidence: A subscriber shall be deemed to have accepted a Digital Signature Certificate if he publishes or authorises the publication

cases.query: What must a subscriber do if a private key has been compromised?
expected_evidence: the subscriber shall communicate the same without any delay to the Certifying Authority

cases.query: What conduct is covered by section 43 concerning unauthorized access?
expected_evidence: without permission of the owner or any other person who is in charge of a computer

cases.query: When is publication of an electronic signature certificate prohibited?
expected_evidence: the certificate has been revoked or suspended

cases.query: When does the Information Technology Act apply to an offence committed outside India?
expected_evidence: the act or conduct constituting the offence or contravention involves a computer, computer system or computer network located in India

cases.query: What is a handloom under the Handlooms Act, 1985?
expected_evidence: handloom means any loom, other than power loom

cases.query: When may the Central Government reserve an article for exclusive production by handlooms?
expected_evidence: after considering the recommendations made to it by the Advisory Committee

cases.query: Why is the Advisory Committee constituted under the Handlooms Act?
expected_evidence: determining the nature of any article or class of articles that may be reserved for exclusive production by handlooms

cases.query: What factors must the Advisory Committee consider?
expected_evidence: the article or class of articles which is being produced traditionally by handlooms

cases.query: What is prohibited once an article has been reserved exclusively for handlooms?
expected_evidence: such article or class of articles shall not, on and from the date of reservation, be produced by any loom, other than handloom

cases.query: What information or samples can the Central Government require from a manufacturer?
expected_evidence: require any manufacturer to furnish

cases.query: What powers does an authorised officer have to inspect a manufacturer's premises?
expected_evidence: may enter, at all reasonable times, any place or premises of any manufacturer

cases.query: When may an authorised officer search and seize under the Handlooms Act?
expected_evidence: he may enter into and search such place or premises

cases.query: Which procedural law applies to searches and seizures under the Handlooms Act?
expected_evidence: The provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, relating to searches and seizures shall, so far as may be, apply

cases.query: What is the penalty for producing articles in contravention of an order under section 3?
expected_evidence: punishable with imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months

cases.query: What constitutes a false statement under the Handlooms Act?
expected_evidence: makes any statement or furnishes any information which is false in any material particular

cases.query: Are offences punishable under the Handlooms Act cognizable?
expected_evidence: every offence punishable under this Act shall be cognizable

cases.query: What protection does the Handlooms Act provide for actions taken in good faith?
expected_evidence: No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against the Central Government, State Government or any officer or employee

cases.query: When can the Central Government exempt an article reserved for handlooms?
expected_evidence: the demand for any article or class of articles reserved by an order under section 3 outside India is such that it is not possible for the handloom industry to meet such demand
